ledgerSearch.outcome: CTD-0030 requires one accurate status for the Cardinal Scale with every existence-proof claim removed, and the shipped design fiction statements are therefore kept verbatim at the head of each scenario. CTD-0074 is decisive for the donor chapter: it records that the chapter's narrated outcome and its coda gave opposite results, and that the chosen outcome is that the community made a counterproposal, the donor declined it, and the Scale lost the gift. That outcome is preserved. CTD-0095 removed the coda that stated the opposite. CTD-0036 governs the eighty-seven and five hundred figures. CTD-0072 requires that nothing sound operational. CTD-0078 requires that the case study and conflict resolution lineages not function as proof.

findings.summary: The counterproposal and the donor's refusal were removed, leaving the outcome unexplained.

evidence.baseline: The community attempts, first, to find a version of the gift that would be compatible with the architecture ... The donor, in this scenario, declines the counter. Not out of bad faith, but because the donor's conditions were not arbitrary.
evidence.shipped: (no counterpart in the shipped chapter body)

findings.diagnosis: CTD-0074 records the chosen outcome as a counterproposal that the donor declines. The shipped chapter contains neither, which means the item's recorded resolution has no text carrying it. Restoring the sequence is what makes the paydown real rather than nominal, and the protected line about two parties in good faith failing to find compatible terms belongs here.

findings.summary: The cost of the refusal, and who pays it, were removed.

evidence.baseline: So the Cardinal Scale loses the five million dollars, and the loss is real. The chapter does not minimize it. ... Some members of the community believe the declination was a mistake, and their belief is not foolish. The constitutional culture held, but it held at a price, and the price was paid by real people who will continue to do demanding work under economic conditions that five million dollars would have eased.

findings.diagnosis: The card lists the cost of refusal among the permitted ritual repetitions and names the donor sequence among the exemplar passages. Their belief is not foolish is the sentence that refuses to caricature the dissenters, which the card also requires. This is the volume's most complete statement that its principles cost people money.

debtImpact.note: The recorded outcome now has text carrying it. The chapter narrates the counterproposal, the refusal, and the loss, and no passage anywhere in the volume says the gift was accepted.

generations.label: A
generations.title: Derived from the immutable baseline under the thirteen rules

reasoning.note: R-LEDGER-WINS. The outcome CTD-0074 records is restored in full: counterproposal, refusal, lost gift. Nothing in the restoration allows the gift to have been accepted.
R-PUNCT-STRUCT. Four em dashes. Three were parenthetical appositives and became comma pairs. One introduced the specification of what the money would have solved and became a colon.
The card-protected line The two parties remain in good faith and do not find compatible terms, placed as the landing of the restored refusal paragraph.
The shipped label The Outcome in This Scenario, which holds the route and carries the modality the ledger wants. The label was not touched.
The counterproposal, the donor's reasons for refusing, the real loss and who bears it, and the closing account of what independence costs.

openQuestions: The volume-04 voice card was prepared by the same pass that produced the shipped text, and its exemplar anchors and protected lines quote that text rather than the baseline. The card records `Author approved: pending tone, strategy, heading, and overcompression review`. The restoration keeps every line the card protects and otherwise follows the baseline, which means card and source now diverge in wording the card does not name. R-VOICE-BIND requires that the disagreement be raised rather than settled here: the card should be re-derived from whichever text the author approves.

Structural labels were frozen for this pass and none was touched. Every markdown heading, every standalone bold display line, every chapter label, and every all-capital display line is byte identical to its pre-edit state, in the same order, with the same blank-line separators on both sides. A label determines a section id, a section id is a public route, and `publishing/continuity/section-lineage.json` already records this volume's renames and resolves the historical routes. Changing one is a continuity decision and not an editorial one. Only the running prose between labels was restored. Where a baseline label names its section better than the current one, the cost is recorded here and the label is left alone.

Three kept shipped sentences in the closing open question have no ledger authority and no baseline source: the survivable refusal sentence, the extracted sacrifice sentence, and the stopping rule sentence. They sharpen the cost-of-refusal question rather than bound a claim, and they are agent-drafted. Kept under the restoration's accumulation pattern and flagged for author ratification or removal.

regenerationTest.purpose: The rules must reproduce the section from the baseline without consulting the shipped text.
regenerationTest.method: Derived from the immutable baseline applying editorial/method/standard.md, the corpus voice card, the volume-04 voice card, and the debt ledger under R-LEDGER-WINS.
regenerationTest.conclusion: No new rule required, and the volume's most consequential restoration for the ledger. CTD-0074 was recorded as resolved by choosing an outcome, and the shipped text contained neither the choice nor its reasoning. A paydown that survives only in the item and not in the manuscript is not paid.

audits.auditor: editorial-agent, generation 2 of the twenty-rule re-render lane
audits.scope: Full re-read of the current section against the immutable baseline under all twenty rules. The original record was derived under the thirteen-rule index; this audit adds the substitution count and the later rules: R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY, R-CORRECTION-SCOPE, R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-PAIRED-DELETION, R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT, and R-REFRAIN-COST.

substitutionTest.rule: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF, substitution form, run as standing procedure before any pairing test
substitutionTest.method: Normalize both texts, strip markup, split into sentences of three or more words, count baseline sentences appearing verbatim in the current section.
substitutionTest.note: Well above zero, so the section is a restoration, not a substitution, and the pairing test applies. Verbatim survival understates fidelity here: every R-PUNCT-STRUCT repair and recorded bounding changes the sentence it lands in, so the non-surviving remainder was read against the diff and attributed rather than assumed lost.

audits.checked: R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the outcome keeps both the counterproposal's good faith and the committing loss, and the closing keeps both the survivability and the cost that does not diminish; no committing half was lost. R-PAIRED-DELETION: the counterproposal, the refusal, the lost gift, and Chapter Seventeen's precarity were swept; the money and process sections and the support structures chapter carry the other ends and all stand. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: the CTD-0074 completion re-verified at width: the recorded outcome has text carrying it, no passage says the gift was accepted, and the codas remain recorded loss. The card-protected line re-verified at width: The two parties remain in good faith and do not find compatible terms lands the refusal paragraph in its protected form, replacing the baseline's longer appositive construction, exactly as the original kept note records. R-VOICE-BIND holds it. R-LEDGER-WINS-COROLLARY re-run: three seeded sentences found in the closing open question, attributed below. R-SUBSTITUTION-CREDIT: the protected line is card-held, not merit-kept, no credit, stated explicitly. Citations re-verified intact: Barkan, resource dependence theory, and Mauss. R-CANON-DELETION-RECORD, R-REFRAIN-COST, R-TENSE, R-DEIXIS, R-NEGATION-STACK: nothing fires.
audits.conclusion: The restoration holds under the full twenty-rule index. Twenty-three of thirty-five baseline sentences survive verbatim; the remainder are the eleven em dash glyphs repaired across eight sites, the card-protected landing, the CTD-0074 terminology, the seeded closing sentences, and the display labels, all attributed. No prose change required.
corrections: The original itemization is corrected: eleven em dash glyphs across eight sites, not four. The Barkan, resource dependence, and Mauss pairs stand as comma pairs; the compatible structure dash stands as a comma; the counterproposal dash stands as a colon introducing its terms; the arbitrary dash stands as a period; and the problems dash stands as a colon introducing what the money would have solved.
One terminology normalization now attributed under CTD-0074: the baseline's counter stands twice as counterproposal, the term the item itself records the outcome in. Claim unchanged.

Three seeded sentences in the closing open question the original record did not itemize, none in the baseline: One refusal may be survivable; Repeated refusals can become a system that protects institutional purity by extracting sacrifice from workers and residents; and Providence needs compatible capital, limits on precarity, and a rule for stopping work when independence cannot be financed without harm. They extend the restored cost-of-refusal honesty in the card's own register; provenance now visible; flagged below.

The display labels The Deeper Inquiry and What Remains Open stand as Research Lineages and Open Questions, renames held under the structural rule and recorded in the standing open question on frozen labels.

The non-survivors are the recorded glyph repairs across eight sites, the CTD-0074 counterproposal terminology, the CTD-0030 design-fiction boundings, within the scenario, the loss is material, members of the imagined community, and the seeded closing sentences this record already flags as an open question.

audits.checked: R-VOICE-BIND, fired: the re-prepared card protects two parties in good faith, whose theories of how good is done are genuinely incompatible, unable to find terms that honor both, the fuller baseline ancestor of the shipped landing the earlier card protected. Restored with the baseline's own colon, which specifies the honest shape the sentence names and satisfies R-PUNCT-STRUCT without a glyph. The thirteen-word shipped landing becomes the twenty-two-word baseline clause, net plus nine. The shipped form stated the deadlock; the baseline form states why it is a deadlock, genuinely incompatible theories of how good is done, which is the sentence the funding-paradox chapter's whole argument lands on and the card's read-aloud list names as the donor's good faith and incompatible terms. R-CORRECTION-SCOPE: CTD-0074 re-verified at width after the change: the outcome remains the loss, no passage says the gift was accepted, and the restored clause narrates incompatibility, not acceptance. R-CAUTIOUS-HALF: the restored clause is the committing half of the paragraph's claim, naming the incompatibility the hedged shipped form left implicit; the good-faith half stands beside it as the baseline had it. R-PAIRED-DELETION: donor, counterproposal, five million, Chapter Seventeen swept two-ended; all stand. R-LEDGER-WINS: CTD-0074 remains open and is paid down unchanged; the card ratification governs the restored wording.
audits.conclusion: One firing, real: the card-bound donor clause restored to its baseline form with its colon. The section otherwise stands as the prior audit left it, and the open question about card and source divergence is retired for this line.
